title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from the previous page: Grothendieck has built a category \hat{C}_0, which he calls 'isotopiques profinis', of ambient algebraic curves over an algebraically closed field k. A morphism between two such curves is described in two ways. Transcendentally, it is a profinite class of paths between points of a suitable modular multiplicity, meaning the moduli stack M_{g,ν} or a level cover of it. Algebraically, it is a finite étale map of curves. Composition mixes two operations: composition in the profinite fundamental groupoid of the moduli stack, and composition of finite étale maps. The construction makes sense over any algebraically closed k, of any characteristic, and is functorial in k.

This page continues the argument:
(1) For an extension k ⊂ k' of algebraically closed fields, the base-change functors (by extension of the base field, applied to the fundamental groupoids and the étale covers) are equivalences of categories. Grothendieck first wrote 'fully faithful but [not] surjective' and then corrected this to equivalences. The marginal note seems to add that the category over k' is equivalent to a category of curves coming from k.
(2) The reason given in the parenthesis: the profinite fundamental groupoid of the relevant moduli multiplicity does not change under extension of the algebraically closed base field. This is the standard invariance of π_1^{ét} in characteristic 0. Implicitly it uses that étale covers of curves over k' descend to k.
(3) Consequence: the automorphism group of k acts on this category. Grothendieck proposes to call it the Teichmüller–Galois category attached to k. For k = \bar{Q} this gives an action of Gal(\bar{Q}/Q). For k = C, Aut(C) acts through the same category, because the categories over \bar{Q} and C are equivalent.
(4) Structure of the category:
- Isomorphism classes of connected objects correspond one-to-one to the topological types (g,ν).
- The automorphism group of an object is, up to inner automorphisms (outer sense), the profinite completion of the standard Teichmüller (mapping class) group Γ_{g,ν}.

The next page stresses two points. First, this is no longer a groupoid: it enlarges the 'Teichmüller–Poincaré' groupoid so as to link curves of different types (g,ν). Second, the programme is to determine this category and its Gal(\bar{Q}/Q)-action by purely algebraic or combinatorial means (maps and cartes). This is an early form of the Teichmüller tower and Galois-action programme later announced in the Esquisse.
errors: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 the étale fundamental group of a non-proper variety, such as an open moduli stack or a punctured curve, is NOT invariant under extension of algebraically closed fields, because of wild ramification. So the equivalence claim (and hence the Aut(k)-action argument) holds only in characteristic 0, or after restricting to prime-to-p data. The page appears to state the equivalence in the characteristic-0 context, but the preceding page asserts that the construction works in any characteristic. This caveat is not spelled out on the visible text.

The automorphism groups are profinite completions of Γ_{g,ν} only for the geometric étale π_1 of the moduli stack. This needs the (true) fact that π_1^{ét}(M_{g,ν}⊗\bar{Q}) is the profinite completion of the topological π_1. The precise identification 'extérieurement' (up to inner automorphisms) is correctly hedged.

ideas.what: Invariance of the étale fundamental groupoid of the moduli stack M_{g,ν} under extension of algebraically closed fields of characteristic 0, giving equivalence of the Teichmüller–Galois categories over k and k'
ideas.modern_name: Invariance of π_1^{ét} under algebraically closed base change (SGA1 XIII), applied to the moduli stacks M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1); for moduli stacks folklore, e.g. Oda, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (general invariance); Esquisse d'un programme (applied to moduli)

ideas.what: Teichmüller–Galois category: objects are curves of all types (g,ν); morphisms combine profinite path classes in the moduli stacks with finite étale maps of curves; Aut(k) (so Gal(\bar{Q}/Q)) acts on it
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Teichmüller tower with Galois action (Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory), here enlarged by covering morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (1984); developed by Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: The Teichmüller tower and Galois action appear in the Esquisse, but with gluing and erasing operations, not explicitly as a category with finite étale morphisms between curves

ideas.what: Connected components of the category correspond to types (g,ν); automorphism groups are profinite completions of the Teichmüller groups Γ_{g,ν}
The category is not a groupoid; it enlarges the Teichmüller–Poincaré groupoid in order to relate curves of different combinatorial types via étale covers
ideas.modern_name: Category of curves with covering morphisms over the Teichmüller groupoid (cf. Hurwitz-space and covering-compatibility of the Galois action)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; related ideas in Boggi, Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki

missed.claim: Grothendieck's object on which Gal(\bar{Q}/Q) acts is not only the tower of profinite mapping class groups linked by gluing and erasing (the Esquisse/GT version). It is a non-groupoid category in which finite étale covers between curves of different types (g,ν) are morphisms. The resulting compatibility of the outer Galois actions on \hat{Γ}_{g,ν} with all covering maps is a stronger, 'covering-functorial' structure than the one standardly studied in GT theory.
missed.quote: Le fait d'avoir élargi le groupoïde des Teichmüller–Poincaré en la catégorie (qui n'est plus un groupoïde !) des Teichmüller–Galois
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests defining a 'GT-type' group as the automorphisms of this enlarged category, i.e. one also compatible with covering maps. It could then be compared with \hat{GT} and with Gal(\bar{Q}/Q). This connects GT theory with anabelian results on morphisms between hyperbolic curves (Mochizuki, Tamagawa) and with congruence-subgroup questions (Boggi). As far as I know, this precise categorical formulation is not standard in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (post-1978) formulation of the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower, which is credited to Grothendieck through the Esquisse. The mildly distinctive point is the non-groupoid enlargement by finite étale covers between curves of different types. The rest is standard.

The struck text is likely 'pl. fidèles' (pleinement fidèles), replaced above by 'des équivalences de cat.'; the bracket reads roughly '[mais [non] essentiellement surjectifs]', with 'essentiellement' struck.
Parenthesis likely: '(Cela provient du fait que le groupoïde fondamental de la multiplicité modulaire pertinente ... ne change pas par extension ... des corps de base alg. clos)'.

Line 'En particulier, le groupe ...' likely reads: 'En particulier, le groupe des automorphismes de k opère sur la catégorie précédente, que j'ai envie d'appeler la catégorie des Teichmüller–Galois associée à k.'
'les groupes d'automorphismes d'un objet sont extérieurement isomorphes aux complétés profinis des groupes de Teichmüller standard' — 'standard' rather than '...'.
Margin likely: 'Mais elle est équivalente à une catégorie de courbes alg. sur k ... provenant de ...'.
